All 9 Evidence Contract measurements are present and corroborated: 400/400 joined on message ID with 0 misses, the header trace ID matches the producer span, 100/100 process spans are linked with receive telemetry on, and 10/10 Splunk traces hold both services.

The lab is careful: the jar SHA is checked unchanged, the agent is pinned to 2.33.1 and its version is checked, receive spans serve as a positive control, and the link is attributed to process spans rather than receive spans.
The repo path in the post's clone command and footer differs from the recorded LAB_URL, so as written a reader may not be able to reproduce it.

The default-run count of receive spans is left out of the post, even though the contract asks for it in both runs. That weakens the claim that one setting changed the shape. Each setting also ran only once, which the post says.

The reader and decision are clear, and the opening delivers what the title promises. The default behaviour is already stated by a maintainer in discussion 14193, so the new value is the per-message count, plus two details: the link sits on the process span, and 100 messages produced 76 receive spans.
The brief's second trade-off is missing. It's the AWSTraceHeader attribute versus the configured propagator in message attributes, and the reader never learns when they'd want the propagator.
Some phrasing reads as generated: 'The trick:', 'Here's how', 'Two details are worth knowing', and TL;DR bullets with an even rhythm. Several code blocks are tidied echo summaries, not a raw session.
The time and cost figures disagree. The TL;DR says about 21 minutes, the steps add up to 17 minutes before destroy, and the lab README says the resources run for about an hour.
The only demand signal is one GitHub discussion, with 5 comments and 15 replies, plus a June 2026 follow-up question. That's real but weak, and there's no search volume data.
The title credits Splunk APM and the OTel Java agent with the answer and names SQS, which is how a reader would search. 'Zero Code' is accurate.
Splunk fits naturally: the service map with the inferred sqs node and the 10/10 trace readback serve the reader. It isn't forced.
A score of 4 would need a stronger signal than one thread, such as reactions or views on this exact question.

claims.text: A maintainer of the Java instrumentation describes AWSTraceHeader propagation as the agent's default
The AWSTraceHeader attribute doesn't count towards message size
The header uses the AWS X-Ray trace header format
The receive telemetry setting is marked experimental
The maintainer discussion notes exceptions for batch receives
Services using SqsTemplate and single-message @SqsListener methods in general will get the same one-trace result from the variable alone
Receive telemetry suits readers who want each consumer's work in a trace of its own

brief.reader: Platform engineer running Spring Boot services on EKS that talk over Amazon SQS
brief.decision: Whether to roll out the OTel Java agent alone for queue tracing, before asking any team for code changes or extra settings
brief.question: With only the Java agent attached, do my SQS producer and consumer land in one trace, and do I need a setting for that?
brief.takeaway: You can follow a message across SQS in Splunk APM from one environment variable, on the OpenTelemetry Java agent's defaults, and you know the one setting that gives each consumer a linked trace of its own.
brief.adds: Existing pages name the settings and describe the system attribute. This post counts real messages on a real queue, shows the header on a waiting message next to the producer span's trace ID, and measures what one setting changes.
brief.open_question: Of 400 messages sent through a real SQS queue with the Java agent on its defaults, what percent have producer and process spans sharing one trace ID, and with receive telemetry on, how many of 100 stay in that trace and how many link to it?
tradeoffs: One trace per message by default, or receive telemetry with each consumer in a linked trace of its own
The AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, or the configured propagator in message attributes

existing_pages.title: Springboot sqs instrumentation
existing_pages.covers: A maintainer explains that context travels in the AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, that producer and consumer should share a trace by default, and that receive telemetry gives separate traces joined by a span link. It gives no per-message count on real SQS.

existing_pages.title: Message metadata for Amazon SQS
existing_pages.covers: Message system attributes, and AWSTraceHeader as the supported one, holding an X-Ray trace header string. It doesn't cover the Java agent.

existing_pages.title: Settings for the AWS SDK instrumentation
existing_pages.covers: The agent's AWS SDK settings and their defaults, including the propagator setting for SNS and SQS, which defaults to false.

existing_pages.title: AWS SDK instrumentation metadata, v2.33.1
existing_pages.covers: The instrumentation's settings at v2.33.1, including receive telemetry, off by default, which starts a new consumer trace with a span link to the producer.

existing_pages.title: Spring Cloud AWS
existing_pages.covers: How to send with SqsTemplate and receive with SqsListener, with its own Observability Support section.
